questions.prompt: You wept for the death of my son all through the night.
questions.answer: Dē morte fīliī meī tōtā nocte flēbās.

questions.prompt: With his own hand the tyrant slew his own children.
questions.answer: Suā manū tyrannus līberōs suōs occīdit.

questions.prompt: Fear of you kept the citizens quiet for many days.
questions.answer: Metus vester cīvēs multōs diēs quiētōs tenuit.

questions.prompt: Longing for you troubled the soldiers stationed on the frontier.
questions.answer: Dēsīderium tuum mīlitēs in fīnibus positōs sollicitābat.

questions.prompt: By my own help the city was freed from great danger.
questions.answer: Meā ipsīus operā urbs magnō perīculō līberāta est.

questions.prompt: By our own effort we defended the walls against the enemy.
questions.answer: Nostrā ipsōrum operā mūrōs contrā hostēs dēfendimus.

questions.prompt: By the assistance of me alone the plan was completed.
questions.answer: Meā ūnīus operā cōnsilium cōnfectum est.

questions.prompt: I love my father, who taught me the art of war.
questions.answer: Patrem amō, quī mē artem bellī docuit.

questions.prompt: Your anger, my friend, has destroyed all our hopes.
questions.answer: Īra tua, amīce, omnēs spēs nostrās dēlēvit.

questions.prompt: For the sake of my safety the friends endured great toils.
questions.answer: Salūtis meae causā amīcī magnōs labōrēs tulērunt.

questions.prompt: Your virtue, not your wealth, wins my praise.
questions.answer: Virtūs tua, nōn dīvitiae, laudem meam meret.

questions.prompt: With their own weapons the captives wounded the guards.
questions.answer: Suīs armīs captīvī custōdēs vulnerāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The memory of you consoles me in these bitter times.
questions.answer: Memoria tua mē hīs temporibus acerbīs cōnsōlātur.

questions.prompt: Our safety depends on your counsel, most wise leader.
questions.answer: Salūs nostra ex cōnsiliō tuō pendet, sapientissime dux.

questions.prompt: The mother wept for the death of her son, slain in battle.
questions.answer: Māter dē morte fīliī suī in proeliō occīsī flēbat.

questions.prompt: Hatred of us drove the exiles across the sea.
questions.answer: Odium nostrum exsulēs trāns mare ēgit.

questions.prompt: By our own judgment we saved the fatherland from ruin.
questions.answer: Nostrā ipsōrum sententiā patriam ā ruīnā servāvimus.

questions.prompt: You feared for the safety of your daughters, hidden in the woods.
questions.answer: Dē salūte fīliārum tuārum in silvīs occultātārum timēbās.

questions.prompt: My own zeal, not fortune, brought this reward.
questions.answer: Meum ipsīus studium, nōn fortūna, hoc praemium attulit.

questions.prompt: In my judgment the ancient laws ought to be preserved.
questions.answer: Meō quidem iūdiciō lēgēs antīquae servārī dēbent.

questions.prompt: Care for you kept the old man awake the whole night.
questions.answer: Cūra tua senem tōtā nocte vigilem tenuit.

questions.prompt: With her own tears the mother softened the stern judge.
questions.answer: Suīs lacrimīs māter iūdicem dūrum mollīvit.

questions.prompt: The longing for you, sweetest wife, sustains me in exile.
questions.answer: Dēsīderium tuum, uxor dulcissima, mē in exiliō sustinet.

questions.prompt: By the labor of me alone the fields were cultivated.
questions.answer: Meā ūnīus operā agrī cultī sunt.

questions.prompt: You praised my father, though you feared his stern words.
questions.answer: Patrem meum laudāvistī, quamquam verba eius sevēra timēbās.

questions.prompt: The fear of you drove the wicked magistrates into exile.
questions.answer: Metus vester magistrātūs improbōs in exilium ēgit.

questions.prompt: By our very own hands we built the temple of the gods.
questions.answer: Nostrīs ipsōrum manibus templum deōrum aedificāvimus.

questions.prompt: I defend my fatherland, which the enemies fiercely attack.
questions.answer: Patriam meam dēfendō, quam hostēs ferōciter oppugnant.

questions.prompt: By my own effort at least the treaty was preserved.
questions.answer: Meā quidem operā foedus servātum est.

questions.prompt: With his own sword the soldier defended the wounded leader.
questions.answer: Suō gladiō mīles ducem vulnerātum dēfendit.

questions.prompt: In my judgment at least, the poet deserves great glory.
questions.answer: Meō quidem iūdiciō poēta magnam glōriam meret.

questions.prompt: The hatred of us stirred the neighboring tribes to war.
questions.answer: Odium nostrum fīnitimās gentēs ad bellum concitāvit.

questions.prompt: You mourned the death of your brother, slain by treachery.
questions.answer: Dē morte frātris tuī flēbās, perfidiā interfectī.

questions.prompt: The Germans led their troops out of the camp.
questions.answer: Germānī suās cōpiās castrīs ēdūxērunt.

questions.prompt: To him who knows not what port he is bound to, no wind is fair.
questions.answer: Īgnōrantī quem portum petat nūllus suus ventus est.

questions.prompt: In a letter of yours.
questions.answer: in tuā quādam epistolā.

questions.prompt: With great personal risk.
questions.answer: magnō suī cum perīculō.
